errors.description: Measured as raw pixel area the buckle-and-strap assembly is about 17% of the frame rather than the literal 40-60% target, because the strap is a thin horizontal band.
errors.expected: Adjuster mechanism at 40-60% of frame area.
errors.actual: The assembly spans roughly 80% of the frame width as the sole subject, with only waistband cloth around it and nothing competing; identifiable in well under one second.
errors.correction: Cropping tighter would cut off the strap ends and destroy the 'how the strap engages the buckle' checklist item. The component-macro intent is met.

errors.description: The three-quarter viewing angle of the blueprint is flattened to a near-frontal macro of the waistband.
errors.expected: Three-quarter front view of the trouser hip.
errors.actual: Near-frontal close macro on the waistband band itself.
errors.correction: Unavoidable consequence of the mandated extreme macro crop; the waistband face shown is the same face the blueprint shows.

lockedFeatures: EXACTLY ONE side-adjuster, no second buckle and no mirrored duplicate - CORRECT
Adjuster set into the WAISTBAND itself, waistband seam lines visible above and below - CORRECT, not on the outseam
Elongated octagonal polished metal buckle frame - CORRECT, a near-exact match to the octagonal red outline in the drawing
Cloth strap passing through the buckle with a central vertical metal bar - CORRECT, matching the small inner rectangle in the drawing
Pointed strap end lying flat beyond the buckle - CORRECT, matching the arrow-like tip in the drawing
Closure FULLY FASTENED, single state, flat and pressed against the waistband - CORRECT
No curled tab, floating extension, twisted band or hanging interior curtain - CORRECT
Component-macro framing with the hardware as the sole subject - CORRECT (attempt 1 was a hip fashion crop at roughly 5%)
No belt loop in frame - CORRECT (a spurious loop appeared on attempt 1)
No pleats, pocket, shirt, hip silhouette or trouser leg in frame - CORRECT
Hardware and cloth in true metal and wool materials, NOT red - CORRECT
Zero annotation: no numbers, arrows, leader lines or text - CORRECT
notes: Attempt 2 fixes the major scale failure from attempt 1 and removes the invented belt loop. The hardware geometry that was already outstanding on attempt 1 is preserved verbatim: the elongated octagonal buckle with a central bar and a pointed strap end is an almost literal reproduction of the red-outlined shape in the blueprint, rendered in polished metal and navy wool with no red anywhere. This now reads as the luxury-hardware macro the option requires.
